published_statement: p.3-4: 'we need to consider a perfect fluid with the energy-momentum tensor T^{mu nu} = (p + rho) u^mu u^nu + p g^{mu nu} (2.1), and with the following spacetime metric in spherical symmetry: ds^2 = -A(r,t)^2 dt^2 + B(r,t)^2 dr^2 + R(r,t)^2 dOmega^2 (2.2) ... we have chosen zero-shift vector beta^i = 0 (comoving threading). The components of the four-velocity ... u^t = 1/A and u^i = 0 ... (comoving slicing).' '(1/A) dR/dt = D_t R = U(r,t), (1/B) dR/dr = D_r R = Gamma(r,t) (2.3), where D_t and D_r are the proper time and distance derivatives.' 'The Misner-Sharp mass M(r,t) is introduced as M(R) = int_0^R 4 pi Rt^2 rho dRt (2.4), which is related with Gamma, U and R through the constraint: Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R) (2.5)'; p.5: 'where Gamma is called the generalised Lorentz factor, which includes the gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy per unit mass.' p.12 (same paper): 'we observe the throat-neck structure in the areal radius R, which causes the function Gamma to take negative values' and 'when Gamma < 0, the integrand in Eq. (2.4) (4 pi Rt^2 rho Gamma B), taken over the comoving radial coordinate r includes a locally "negative mass" component'. Units G = c = 1 (p.3).
published_hypotheses: H1 spherical symmetry, metric (2.2) diagonal in (t, r)
H2 zero shift beta^i = 0 ('comoving threading') -- makes D_t = (1/A) d_t the derivative along the slice normal
H3 perfect fluid (2.1), comoving slicing u^t = 1/A (no radial energy flux in these coordinates)
H4 M defined by the integral (2.4) from R = 0 (regular centre implied); taken over r with integrand 4 pi R^2 rho Gamma B when R is non-monotonic (p.12)
H5 Einstein field equations (the constraint (2.5) is stated as following from them: 'Solving the Einstein field equations, the following quantities appear')
H6 IMPLICIT in the printed root of (2.5): Gamma >= 0, i.e. R' > 0 with outward-oriented r -- a hypothesis the same paper departs from on p.12 (Gamma < 0 for type-II data)

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on this result in either direction, and the evidence is structural: (2.3) is a definition and (2.5), with M the geometric Misner-Sharp mass, is an identity of the metric (check A, residual 0) into which no measured quantity enters -- there is no datum the author could have lacked. What the source DID lack is not data but a named hypothesis: the printed positive root silently assumes R' > 0, which the type-I literature it inherits from always satisfied, and which the paper's own type-II subject (p.12, Gamma < 0) violates. That omission is a presentation discrepancy in the source (the squared constraint, which is what the numerics and the tree's computation use, is correct on both branches), not a physical error. The later paper 2505.00366 (same group) writes the two-branch form explicitly. So: no moved datum; one unnamed branch hypothesis, inherited by the tree's prose.
grade_evidence: READ at source (2504.05813v3 pp.3-5, 12). The definitions (2.3) and the constraint in SQUARED form, Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R, STAND for every use the tree makes and hold more generally than the source's perfect-fluid/comoving hypotheses once M is the geometric Misner-Sharp mass, as the tree defines it (check A; driven.py:541-548; driven.py V4 and contracts() use only the square). The name 'generalised Lorentz factor' is quoted accurately. The narrowing is the printed root: 'Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R)' (quoted at driven.py:75, implemented at driven.py:376-381) holds only where Gamma >= 0 (R' > 0, outward r), and the source's own p.12 has Gamma < 0; 2505.00366 p.4 writes +-sqrt(1+2E). Carried into the tree, the chain 'dl < dR <=> Gamma > 1 <=> 2m/R < U^2' (driven.py:164, 386; also 78-80, 512, 891) is shown false on the far side of a throat (check D: Gamma = -1.997505, contracts() True, Gamma > 1 and dl < dR False). This is NOT WRONG: no computed result of the tree's is refuted -- contracts() computes the orientation-free |dR| > dl, V1-V8 residuals are unaffected, and on R' > 0 the chain holds (D5). It is a hypothesis (R' > 0 / positive branch) the tree drops, on a class (spacetimes with throats) the tree applies it to. Recorded, not repaired.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names R' > 0 (outward-oriented r, no neck on the slice) as the hypothesis of every 'Gamma > 1' / '+sqrt' statement, or rewrites those statements as |Gamma| > 1 / Gamma^2 > 1 (which is what contracts() already computes) -- nothing in the source would then be used beyond its reach. To WRONG: only a counterexample to the SQUARED identity with geometric M in a diagonal spherically symmetric metric, which check A excludes symbolically. To OPEN: none -- the source was read and the claim is closed-form.
